title: Mechanical Energy
subtitle: Stored energy and moving energy, and the trade between them.
objectives: Explain how energy converts between the two forms
Explain why speed matters more than mass for kinetic energy
Apply mechanical energy to a real situation

cards.title: Energy is not used up. It moves and it changes form
cards.text: Mechanical energy comes in two kinds: the energy of position and the energy of motion. Most of what you watch is one turning into the other.

cards.title: Stored energy, waiting
cards.text: Lift something and you have put energy into it. Let go and you get it back.
points: **Gravitational potential energy** depends on mass and height.
**Twice as high** means twice the stored energy.
**A stretched spring** stores it too, as elastic potential energy.
**Nothing is moving.** The energy is in the arrangement.

cards.title: The energy of actually moving
cards.text: Anything with mass that is moving has kinetic energy. Stopping it means taking that energy somewhere.
points: **It depends on mass and speed**, but not equally.
**Double the mass** and kinetic energy doubles.
**Double the speed** and it goes up four times.
**Speed is squared.** Mass is not.

cards.title: The square law, again
cards.text: You met this with meteors and wind. It is the same rule and it never stops being important.
points: **At 60 km/h** a car carries four times the energy it has at 30.
**Braking distance** follows, which is why speed limits matter so much.
**A heavier car at the same speed** is only proportionally worse.
**Speed is the dangerous variable.** Every time.

question.text: You double a car's speed. Its kinetic energy becomes…
question.explain: Kinetic energy goes with speed squared. Doubling speed quadruples the energy that has to go somewhere.

cards.title: One turns into the other, over and over
cards.text: Drop something and height turns into speed. Throw it up and speed turns back into height.
points: **At the top** of a throw: maximum potential, zero kinetic.
**At the bottom** of a drop: maximum kinetic, minimum potential.
**Halfway**, it is sharing between the two.
**Friction takes a cut** each time, as heat.

cards.title: Every jump arc in a game is this sum
cards.text: The physics engine is tracking the swap between height and speed, frame by frame.
points: **Rising**, speed falls and height grows.
**At the peak**, vertical speed is zero for an instant.
**Falling**, height converts back into speed.
**Turn gravity down** in a sandbox and the whole arc stretches.

question.text: At the very top of a ball's flight, it has no energy.
question.explain: It has maximum potential energy. Only its kinetic energy is momentarily zero.

cards.title: A fan keeps its energy in the blades
cards.text: Switch a fan off and it does not stop. The blades keep turning for several seconds.
points: **That is kinetic energy** stored in spinning mass.
**Friction in the bearings** is what finally removes it.
**Heavier blades coast longer** — more mass, more stored energy.
**Dry bearings stop it fast**, which is a useful thing to notice.

terms.def: The energy something has because it is moving.
Stored energy, from position or from being stretched.
Energy changing from one form into another.

cards.title: What to remember
points: Potential is stored. Kinetic is moving.
Doubling mass doubles energy. Doubling speed quadruples it.
A drop or a throw is the two forms trading places.
Friction quietly takes a share as heat each time.

quiz.text: Kinetic energy is the energy of…
quiz.explain: Anything with mass that is moving has it.

quiz.text: Lifting a box onto a shelf gives it…
quiz.explain: Height and mass store energy you get back if it falls.

quiz.text: Doubling an object's speed changes its kinetic energy by a factor of…
quiz.explain: Speed is squared in the kinetic energy relationship, so two becomes four.
quiz.objective: Explain why speed matters more than mass for kinetic energy

quiz.text: Doubling an object's mass changes its kinetic energy by a factor of…
quiz.explain: Mass is proportional. Only speed is squared.
quiz.objective: Explain why speed matters more than mass for kinetic energy

quiz.text: At the top of a thrown ball's arc, its kinetic energy is momentarily zero.
quiz.explain: Vertical motion stops for an instant. Potential energy is at its maximum there.
quiz.objective: Explain how energy converts between the two forms

quiz.explain: Height is spent and speed is gained all the way down.
quiz.objective: Explain how energy converts between the two forms

quiz.text: Why do fan blades keep spinning after you switch it off?
options: They hold kinetic energy until friction removes it
quiz.explain: Spinning mass stores energy, and bearing friction is what finally takes it away.
quiz.objective: Apply mechanical energy to a real situation

quiz.text: Where does the lost mechanical energy usually go?
quiz.explain: Friction converts it to heat. Nothing is destroyed, it just changes form.
quiz.objective: Explain how energy converts between the two forms

quiz.explain: The sum of the two mechanical forms.

quiz.text: A heavier car is as dangerous at speed as a faster one.
quiz.explain: Mass is proportional, speed is squared. Speed raises the energy far more sharply.
quiz.objective: Explain why speed matters more than mass for kinetic energy

quiz.explain: Energy is stored in the arrangement, released when it springs back.

quiz.text: Halfway down a fall, the object has…
quiz.explain: It is partway through the trade, so both forms are present.
quiz.objective: Explain how energy converts between the two forms

teacher.summary: Term 2 Week 7 Science. Kinetic and potential energy, with the square law given its own card because it is the single most transferable idea in the week and he has met it twice before, with meteors and with wind. The fan coasting after switch-off is there as a piece of stored kinetic energy he can watch at home and time. Friction's cut is mentioned every time conversion is discussed so energy does not look like it is being destroyed.
discussion: Why is speed more dangerous than mass?
Where is the energy at the top of a throw?
Why do heavier blades coast longer?
extension: Time how long a fan coasts on each speed setting after switch-off.
Drop a ball and watch each bounce come back lower. Where did that energy go?
misconceptions: That something at the top of its flight has no energy.
That energy is used up rather than converted.
That mass and speed matter equally.
